title: Web Crawler
summary: Crawl the web with a distributed, polite fleet of fetchers coordinated through a URL frontier.
narrative:
A web crawler is a deceptively simple loop wrapped around a brutal scaling problem. Start with a handful of seed URLs, fetch each page, pull the links out of it, and repeat — forever, across billions of pages, without ever fetching the same URL twice or hammering any single site into the ground.

The heart of the design is the frontier: a message queue holding the URLs still to be visited. An operator seeds it through a coordinator, and a fleet of stateless worker fetchers pulls URLs off the queue, downloads each page, and pushes the newly discovered links back onto the frontier. Add more workers and you crawl faster; that is the whole point of decoupling the queue from the fetchers.

Two things keep the loop honest. Before fetching, every worker checks a Bloom filter of URLs already seen — a probabilistic set that answers "have we crawled this?" in constant space across tens of billions of URLs. And every page has two homes: the raw bytes land in blob storage, while the processed, searchable content is written to a search index. Wire the loop, and the crawl runs itself.

functional: Fetch pages starting from a set of seed URLs
Discover and enqueue new links found on each page
Skip URLs that have already been crawled
Store raw pages and index their processed content
nonFunctional: Never crawl the same URL twice
Scale throughput by adding more fetchers
Stay polite so no single host is overwhelmed
constraints: Seed URLs enter the frontier only through the coordinator
Only workers fetch pages and write to storage
capacity: Tens of billions of unique URLs tracked
specs.tradeoff: A Bloom filter trades a tiny false-positive rate for constant-time dedup across billions of URLs, avoiding a giant exact set.
specs.bonus: Add Monitoring & Alerting to track fetch rate, frontier queue depth, and per-host politeness.

missions.label: Seed and control the crawl through the Coordinator

Let the fetcher fleet pull URLs off the frontier

topologyRules.message: Operators steer the crawl through the Coordinator, never the fetcher fleet directly.
Seed URLs must enter the frontier through the Coordinator, not be injected straight into the queue.
A page only reaches storage after a Worker has fetched it from the frontier.

resilienceRules.message: Run a fleet of at least two fetchers; a crawler with one worker barely crawls.
Every fetcher must consult the Bloom Filter, or the crawl loops on URLs it has already seen.

hints: Model the crawl as a loop: the Client seeds the Coordinator (Web Server), which fills the Message Queue frontier; Workers pull URLs, fetch pages, and push new links back onto the queue.
Before fetching, every Worker must check the Bloom Filter so the crawl doesn't re-download URLs it has already seen.
Store the raw pages in Blob Storage and the processed, searchable content in the Search Index -- and run a fleet of at least two Workers.
